# Cohort retention triangle

Contents: [Use cases](#use-cases), [Chart IDs](#chart-ids), [Minimal spec](#minimal-spec), [Data](#data), [Options](#options), [Annotations](#annotations), [Exclude a running period](#exclude-a-running-period), [Cumulative conversion from counts](#cumulative-conversion-from-counts), [Sizing](#sizing), [Fixtures](#fixtures), [Not for](#not-for).

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-reference.mjs from the boardplot describe, list and fixtures payloads. -->

Cohorts by periods-since-start: counts in, every retention rate derived, weighted averages that are never the mean of percentages. Type `cohort`. Aliases: `retention`.

## Use cases

- Retention by signup cohort
- Repeat purchase by first month
- Subscription churn by start month

## Chart IDs

- `cohort.heatmap`: fixture `saas-logo-retention`
- `cohort.pure`: fixture `retention-pure-exhibit`
- `cohort.stepped`: fixture `retention-stepped-column`

## Minimal spec

```json
{
  "type": "cohort",
  "data": {
    "periodLabel": "Month",
    "cohorts": [
      { "id": "jan", "label": "Jan 2026", "active": [100, 70, 60], "size": 100 },
      { "id": "feb", "label": "Feb 2026", "active": [80, 60], "size": 80 }
    ]
  },
  "options": {
    "unit": "% of cohort base",
    "title": "January retains 60% of its customers at month two",
    "source": "Illustrative data"
  }
}
```

## Data

| Path | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| periodLabel | string |  | Period unit, e.g. 'Month' -> columns M0, M1, ...; omitted gives 'Period 0'. |
| cohorts | array | yes | At least two cohorts in chronological order, oldest first. |
| cohorts[].id | string | yes | Unique cohort identity; the computed average-row id is reserved. |
| cohorts[].label | string |  | Displayed cohort name; defaults to its id. |
| cohorts[].active | array | yes | Whole nonnegative active-member counts from period zero onward; null is a missing count. The first count must be a known positive cohort base; shorter rows leave later periods unobserved. |
| cohorts[].size | integer |  | Declared cohort base; VERIFIED against active[0], never used in its place. |

## Options

| Path | Type | Values | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| format | string |  |  | Rate format in percentage units, such as '1.0%' or '1.00' for two decimals without a sign on exhibit tables. Default: a decimal below 10%, whole percent otherwise on the heatmap. Exhibit tables share the needed decimal precision. The M0 anchor is neutral and the colour scale stays fixed at 0–100%. |
| basis | string | `'cohort'`, `'previous'` | `'cohort'` | 'cohort' = active / cohort base (comparable down a column); 'previous' = active / the previous period's active. |
| averages | false \| string | `false`, `'weighted'` | `false` | Weighted column average = total active / total base of the observed cohorts. |
| methodNote | boolean |  |  | Default false. true adds the measure formula and explains the visible anchor column and blank cells. strings.cohortMeasure and strings.cohortFormula name another count-based measure, such as cumulative conversion. Required interpretation notes still print: the formula under basis 'previous', not-meaningful cells, weighted averages and rates too narrow to print. |
| variant | string | `'heatmap'`, `'pure'`, `'stepped'` | `'heatmap'` | Form. 'heatmap' (the default) draws the heatmap surface, which honours 'labels'. 'pure' and 'stepped' draw the exhibit. Stepped columns fit measured content, normally 56–72px, and preserve weighted-average and missing-cell notes. The exhibit variants draw a fixed label set, so authoring 'labels' together with variant is refused (the legacy surface honours it). |
| formatScope | string | `'classic'`, `'column'` |  | Stepped fills use absolute bins ('classic') or normalize within each period ('column'). |
| steps | array |  |  | Four ascending thresholds in percentage points that split the absolute ('classic') stepped fills into five classes the key names, such as [70, 80, 85, 90] for period-to-period retention. Default [30, 40, 50, 60]. |
| visiblePeriods | array |  |  | Original zero-based period indices displayed in chronological order by exhibit presets. |
| cohortSizeLabel | string |  |  | Header for the exhibit cohort-size column; defaults to Cohort size. |
| showPercentSign | boolean |  |  | Print a percent sign in every exhibit cell; defaults to false because the unit is stated once. |
| threshold | number \| false | `false` (or another value of its type) |  | Pure-exhibit emphasis threshold in percentage points: cohort and total rates above it print bold; period 0 stays neutral. A note prints only when a visible cell uses that emphasis. Defaults to 60; false disables emphasis and its note. |
| designatedPeriod | integer |  |  | Original zero-based period index receiving the pure-exhibit column tint; defaults to 3. |
| total | false \| string | `false`, `'weighted'` |  | Exhibit summary row: weighted retention by default, or false to hide it. Never averages cohort percentages equally. |
| excludeCurrentPeriod | boolean |  |  | Remove the newest cohort and longest period before exhibit derivation. |
| exhibitLabel | string |  |  | Short exhibit heading above the assertion title. |

Plus the [shared options](options.md). This type does not accept `detailFields`, `categoryLabels`, `valueAxis`, `categoryAxis`, `secondaryAxis`, `rowLabels`, `topN`, `bandFraction`, `colorblindSafe`, `rounding`.

## Annotations

This type takes no annotations.

## Exclude a running period

On exhibit tables, `excludeCurrentPeriod: true` removes the newest cohort and the last observation of each earlier cohort. A disclosure names the removed cohort and explains both removals. Every render target keeps this disclosure with `footnotes: false`.

The disclosure also appears in `reading.notes`. It does not add structured records for removed cells. `visiblePeriods` is a separate display filter.

## Cumulative conversion from counts

Set `strings.cohortMeasure` to the measure name and `strings.cohortFormula` to its formula sentence. The strings change the notes, key caption and accessible description. They do not change the calculation.

Automatic exhibit formats keep the default rounding. A nonzero rate that would print as zero gets only the extra decimals needed to show a nonzero digit. Other rates keep their precision. Authored formats stay unchanged. A pure exhibit uses scientific notation for a zeroed rate only when its decimal text cannot fit.

Bare rate cells get their unit once, in a header line that already exists: the stepped key caption ("Retention in %"), or the corner cell above the cohort labels in pure tables and stepped tables without a key. The default is `%`. A visible classic key keeps an authored unit there. Only structured fields count as showing the unit: `unitShown: true`, a value format that prints it, a custom measure or subtitle measure that names it, or `unit` with a subtitle. A % in the title or in another subtitle field does not count. If fitting cuts the subtitle, the header still names the unit. The table size, calculations and number formatting do not change.

Keep `basis: "cohort"`. Put the eligible cohort count in `active[0]` and the cumulative converted count in each later period. Boardplot divides each later count by `active[0]`. Set `visiblePeriods` to the later periods so the base column does not appear as a conversion result. Short rows leave later periods unobserved. The fixtures `cumulative-conversion-pure` and `cumulative-conversion-stepped` show both exhibit styles.

```json
{
  "type": "cohort",
  "data": {
    "periodLabel": "Week",
    "cohorts": [
      { "id": "a", "label": "Batch A", "active": [1000, 5, 12] },
      { "id": "b", "label": "Batch B", "active": [800, 4] }
    ]
  },
  "options": {
    "title": "Cumulative conversion rises by the second week",
    "variant": "stepped",
    "formatScope": "classic",
    "basis": "cohort",
    "unit": "%",
    "visiblePeriods": [1, 2],
    "steps": [0.5, 1, 2, 3],
    "methodNote": true,
    "size": { "width": 1100 },
    "strings": {
      "cohortMeasure": "Cumulative conversion",
      "cohortFormula": "Cumulative conversion = converted so far / cohort base."
    }
  }
}
```

## Sizing

Floor 280 × 28 px; fit `content`.

Below the floor a render is refused with `size-below-floor` and the pixels it needs. `measure` returns the natural and comfortable size for a given spec; see [Sizing in the manual](../manual.md#sizing).

## Not for

Precomputed retention percentages; cohort takes active-member counts and derives the rates.
